title: Historic Curl flaw shows AI risk to legacy supply chain
key_facts: Curl maintainers released version 8.23.0 on 14 Oct 2026, fixing 24 security vulnerabilities, 18 from a yearlong AI-powered audit by security firm Aisle.
Aisle's models found 35 CVEs and 160 bugs over the engagement.
CVE-2026-8932 is a 25-year-old authentication bypass in connection reuse, present since February 2001.
Curl software runs on more than 20 billion devices.
Daniel Stenberg, Curl's founder and lead, had suspended the bug bounty at the start of 2026 over low-quality reports, but says Aisle's findings were validated.
Aisle checked each finding against current code, had a researcher review it, and Curl's team reproduced reports independently.
quote_evidence: On Oct. 14, Curl maintainers released version 8.23.0, fixing 24 total security vulnerabilities -- 18 of which stem from an extended AI-powered audit by security firm Aisle.
The key takeaway [of the report] is that modern AI-powered code analyzers find flaws in ways nothing did previously.
why_it_matters_hint: AI audits are finding bugs in very old, trusted software, so defenders must update and triage faster.
notes: Released version and counts from TechTarget; the number of CVEs differs in framing (24 fixed in release, 35 over the engagement).
